title: One-Hit Wonders & Forgotten Debuts
theme: The 90s R&B artists who had one brilliant moment — and what happened next
narrativePurpose: Invert the EP001 format — test players not on landmark arrivals but on the artists who arrived, flashed, and faded. Rewards obsessives over casual listeners by Round 2.
toneProgression: Identify the artist from the hit → what was behind it and what came after → formation stories and forgotten infrastructure

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-9-3 — the year the genre minted its most footnotes. Silk's Freak Me hit #1, H-Town's Knockin' Da Boots followed, and a dozen acts peaked and vanished within eighteen months. The most concentrated one-hit-wonder harvest in 90s R&B.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: You know the song. But do you know who made it? Identify the artist from their one big moment.

questions.question: 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' was the 1991 breakout smash for which R&B group?

metadata.song: I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)
metadata.fact: 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1991, making Hi-Five one of the most unlikely chart-toppers of the new jack swing era.
metadata.storyHook: Five teenagers from Waco, Texas — the last place anyone expected a #1 R&B record to come from.

questions.question: 'Freak Me' was the 1993 chart-topping debut single for which R&B group?

metadata.fact: 'Freak Me' spent four weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993 — Silk's commercial peak and the record that defined their career.
metadata.storyHook: Discovered and developed by Michael Bivins — the New Edition alumni machine at full speed.

questions.question: Which duo had their only major US hit with 'Tell Me' in 1995, featuring vocalist Amel Larrieux?

metadata.fact: 'Tell Me' reached #7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995. Groove Theory never released a follow-up album, and Amel Larrieux eventually launched a solo career.
metadata.storyHook: One album. One hit. And then Amel Larrieux disappeared — until she didn't.

questions.question: 'Knockin' Da Boots' was the 1993 debut hit for which Texas-based R&B trio?

metadata.fact: 'Knockin' Da Boots' reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993 and established H-Town as one of Houston's first R&B exports.
metadata.storyHook: Houston's first statement to the national R&B chart — three years before anyone started paying attention to the city.

questions.question: 'Nobody Knows' was the 1996 breakout and commercial peak for which artist — a solo project named after its singer?

metadata.fact: 'Nobody Knows' peaked at #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996 and won a Grammy for Best R&B Song. Tony Rich never replicated its commercial success.
metadata.storyHook: A solo act named like a collective. A Grammy winner who became a trivia answer.

questions.question: Which R&B harmony group peaked with 'If I Ever Fall in Love' in 1992 and never replicated that commercial success?

metadata.song: If I Ever Fall in Love
metadata.album: If I Ever Fall in Love
topicTags: If I Ever Fall in Love
metadata.fact: 'If I Ever Fall in Love' reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1992 and was recorded almost entirely a cappella — a choice that became its defining characteristic.
metadata.storyHook: Four Howard University students. No instruments. One of 1992's biggest records.

questions.question: Zhané — the duo behind 1994's 'Hey Mr. DJ' — were given their first recording break by which rap collective?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — WHO GAVE ZHANÉ THEIR BREAK

metadata.fact: Flavor Unit — Queen Latifah's management collective — discovered Zhané and helped them secure their Motown deal, connecting New Jersey hip-hop infrastructure to R&B.
metadata.storyHook: Queen Latifah's collective handed two R&B singers their entire career. The music business in one sentence.

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: Who was behind the hit. Where they came from. What happened after. The follow-up failures and the infrastructure that built the moment.

questions.question: Hi-Five — the group behind 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' — came from which Texas city rarely associated with 90s R&B?

metadata.fact: Hi-Five formed in Waco, Texas — not a city associated with R&B infrastructure, label connections, or music industry access — which made their national breakthrough even more unlikely.
metadata.storyHook: Not Houston. Not Dallas. Waco — which makes this story more improbable the more you think about it.

questions.question: Silk — the group behind 'Freak Me' — were developed and mentored by which New Edition alumnus?

metadata.fact: Michael Bivins discovered and developed Silk as part of his pattern of mentoring emerging R&B acts — he had already done the same for Boyz II Men and Another Bad Creation.
metadata.storyHook: Michael Bivins built a side career out of developing the groups New Edition never became.

questions.question: Groove Theory vocalist Amel Larrieux eventually launched a solo career with which 2000 debut album?

metadata.fact: After Groove Theory went quiet, Amel Larrieux built a respected solo career entirely outside the mainstream — Infinite Possibilities is considered a quiet neo-soul classic.
metadata.storyHook: She escaped the one-hit wonder label by refusing to chase the hit.

questions.question: H-Town — the trio behind 'Knockin' Da Boots' — were from which Texas city?

metadata.fact: H-Town — brothers Keven 'Dino' Conner and Solomon 'Shazam' Conner, plus Darryl 'G' Jackson — were from Houston, making them part of the city's first wave of national R&B recognition.

questions.question: The R&B group Shai took their name from a word meaning 'gift' in which ancient language?

metadata.fact: Shai is a Hebrew word meaning 'gift' — the group chose the name while students at Howard University, connecting their identity to their academic and cultural environment.
metadata.storyHook: A Hebrew word chosen by four students at an HBCU — the kind of detail that gets lost when the music fades.

questions.question: H-Town's debut album — which contained 'Knockin' Da Boots' — was titled what?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — H-TOWN'S DEBUT ALBUM TITLE

metadata.fact: Fever for da Flavor was released in 1993 on Luke Records — the Miami-based label that gave Houston's H-Town their national platform.
metadata.storyHook: A Houston group. A Miami label. A Waco-level upset on the national R&B chart.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: Formation stories. Forgotten label homes. Debut facts buried under one hit. Only the obsessives survive here.

questions.question: Portrait — the four-man harmony group behind 1992's 'Here We Go Again' — were signed to which major label?

metadata.fact: Portrait's self-titled debut was released on Capitol Records in 1992 — the label pushed 'Here We Go Again' as their breakout single, and it remains the group's only significant chart entry.
metadata.storyHook: Capitol Records had a smooth R&B quartet from Los Angeles and nowhere to go after the first single.

sources.title: Here We Go Again! (Portrait song) – Wikipedia

questions.question: Shai formed while all four members were students at which historically Black university in Washington D.C.?

metadata.fact: All four members of Shai — Carl Martin, Marc Nelson, Darnell Van Rensalier, and Geoffrey Williams — met as students at Howard University, one of the most prominent HBCUs in the country.
metadata.storyHook: Four Howard students made one of 1992's biggest records and then went back to their lives. The record stayed.

questions.question: Hi-Five's self-titled debut album was released in what year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — YEAR HI-FIVE'S DEBUT DROPPED

metadata.fact: Hi-Five's self-titled debut was released in 1990 on Jive Records — 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' didn't become a hit until 1991, making the album's timeline slightly counterintuitive.
metadata.storyHook: The album dropped in 1990. The world didn't hear it until 1991. One year's difference, one chart-topping record.
